title: A local flag does not release a host modal handler
environment: Blender 5.2.1 tested import path. Arbitrary dialog clicking and normal UI Undo remained unverified; no universal native-crash fix is claimed.
goal: Finish foreground import and return safely to normal editor interaction.
approach: Historical failed assumption: The same operator opened a dialog while its preparation modal remained registered; clearing a Python flag was treated as handler removal.
what_worked: Historical correction: Return FINISHED to end preparation in the host, then start separate dialog/prepared operators on later event-loop turns. Bound session lifetime and clean success, cancel and exception paths. Verification reported by the source: Corrected foreground import finished without the preparation handler; 100 interaction cycles and two distinct serial sessions completed with process exit zero and no new crash dump. An invalid timer-context Undo probe was excluded.
what_failed: Historical observed failure: Import completed, then ordinary view interactions caused a native access violation with a modal-callback stack.
why: Confirmed lifecycle defect: host-owned modal registration survived the local flag change and execution reentered the same object.
improved_method: End the host-owned lifecycle before reentrant phase changes. Verify post-completion interaction and host state rather than a local Boolean.
when_to_use: Blender 5.2.1 tested import path. Arbitrary dialog clicking and normal UI Undo remained unverified; no universal native-crash fix is claimed.
when_not_to_use: Do not extrapolate outside the recorded conditions or use partial evidence to claim general product or release acceptance.
known_limitations: This is an independently curated generalization of an earlier recorded failure. No source-side experiment was rerun during this registration; observation_date is the 2026-10-09 knowledge-review date, not the incident date. Applicability and root-cause claims remain limited to the source-reported conditions.
